races.name: Gold & Silver Exchange Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Luminous Warrior
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on good ground eight days ago in fine form, but this drop to 6f on a sharp track is a significant trip concern for a horse who has never run at this trip; hold-up style means he arrives late and needs the race to be run truly.

runners_data.name: Shades Of May
runners_data.note: Mapped to lead as the only pace-setter in the race, though her natural style is prominent-to-hold-up, so she is operating outside her comfort zone; has only two runs on similar ground in 15 outings and her trainer has a modest recent record (1/5 over 14 days).

runners_data.name: Alafdhal
runners_data.note: Veteran of eight who carries the lowest similar-going strike rate in the field (1 from 15), has headgear for a visor, and though his true style is hold-up he is likely to find himself running in midfield — his recent form string of 570765 gives little encouragement.

runners_data.name: So Grateful
runners_data.note: Course and distance form on good ground is the standout angle here — four of his last five runs have been over 5-6f on good, producing a 1W3P record, and he is likely to end up closer than his natural hold-up style dictates given the race shape.

runners_data.name: Endowed
runners_data.note: Trainer John & Rhys Flint in good recent form (3/10 over 14 days) and this nine-year-old has course experience, but the hold-up style is genuinely compromised by being pushed into midfield, and his form string of 279-67 shows nothing at the top of the market.

runners_data.name: Indy's Angel
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a solid profile over 6f on good ground (finishing 2nd twice in her last three at the trip), and though she is a natural hold-up horse nudged forward in the map, her recent form trend is the most encouraging among the hold-up brigade.

runners_data.name: Coiled
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish, has finished 8th, 8th, 11th, 10th and 11th in her last five starts, all on good or similar ground; headgear (t/b) has not unlocked any improvement, and even if the race sets up for late closers this record offers no confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Shades Of May is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this 6f handicap on good-to-firm ground at Yarmouth, redistributed to the front because no other horse naturally wants to lead — she will bowl along from the gates and set a measured, uncontested tempo that is unlikely to be truly severe. The remainder of the field — Luminous Warrior, Alafdhal, So Grateful, Endowed, Indy's Angel and Coiled — are all genuine hold-up types, meaning Shades Of May will have the run of the race from the front without any pressure through the early or middle stages. This field holds far more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate at the rear; So Grateful, Endowed, Indy's Angel and Alafdhal are most likely to end up bunched in midfield rather than settled in their preferred position off the bridle at the back. A sustainable, lone-leader gallop on fast ground at a sharp flat track like Yarmouth strongly favours any horse who can travel prominently or make a forward move early in the straight, as the hold-up brigade will have plenty of ground to make up and a potentially slow-run race to chase down.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Shades Of May Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Shades Of May breaks well and establishes a comfortable lead with no rival willing or able to press her through the early stages.
scenarios.body: She sets a controlled pace that keeps the hold-up horses chasing from halfway, and the fast ground at Yarmouth rewards a horse who can control her own rhythm without burning out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Finish Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough, or if the ground rides quicker than expected, allowing hold-up horses to close with momentum in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A true-run race would compress the finish and give the fitter hold-up types a window to pounce, but most of these closers are racing out of their natural position and may not find their usual rhythm.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed hold-up types — particularly Indy's Angel or So Grateful — manages to sit closer than usual and capitalises on a moderate gallop with a well-timed run.
scenarios.body: Both have strong recent form over similar trips on good ground and could benefit from being handier than expected if the field bunches; Indy's Angel's profile over 6f on good going is particularly relevant here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Winner Unwinds
scenarios.trigger: If Shades Of May goes too hard for her comfort level and fades badly inside the final two furlongs, scrambling the race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: The field lacks a natural second-in-command to take up the running cleanly, which could create a messy finish; Coiled's fade-in-finish flag makes it an unlikely beneficiary even in this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Shades Of May is racing outside her natural style as a hold-up horse redistributed to lead — if she fails to break cleanly or is headed early, the race loses its pace-setter entirely and the shape collapses.

So Grateful has the strongest similar-going form record in the field (8/15 runs, 1W3P on good) — watch whether Miss Brotherton positions her closer than her tag suggests, as that would dramatically improve her chance in a slow-run race.

Indy's Angel has finished 2nd in two of her last three runs over 6f on good ground and represents the most likely threat to emerge from the hold-up group; watch how Mr Loughnane (7lb claim) positions her in the early stages.

Coiled's fade-in-finish flag combined with a form string of 88-000 in her last five means she is the highest-risk banker in any combination — her presence in midfield effectively removes her from winning calculations in any scenario.

Luminous Warrior arrives on the back of a win eight days ago but has never raced at 6f — if the pace is slow and the race is won by a horse who travels prominently, his hold-up style over a trip he has never tried becomes a compounding disadvantage.

races.name: British Stallion Studs Ebf Maiden Fillies' Stakes (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Ava Louise
runners_data.note: Showed modest form (5th, 8th) at 5-6f on Good ground with Hector Crouch up for a small yard; her natural game is to come from well off the pace, but in a field loaded with hold-up types she is unlikely to secure the rear berth she needs and may find herself trapped in traffic mid-division.

runners_data.name: Babzini
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton sends her back after 75 days off with a placing on her CV over 5f; she is a genuine hold-up filly by inclination, yet the sheer number of closers in this field means Charles Bishop may have to take a more forward position than ideal, diluting the late-run threat.

runners_data.name: Divine Concerto
runners_data.note: One run only, a well-beaten ninth over 7f on Good ground, with a flag on fading in the finish; Dylan Cunha's filly is a hold-up type by nature who will need to operate closer to the pace here given the crowded tail, and her tendency to fade makes her an unlikely beneficiary of this shape.

runners_data.name: Foxsbrush
runners_data.note: Seventh on debut over 7f at Newmarket on Good ground for the small John Ryan yard; stepping back to 6f could sharpen her up, but she carries the same hold-up profile and a low trainer 14-day strike rate gives little confidence this is a planned raid.

runners_data.name: Lady Of Hay
runners_data.note: The sole pace-setter here, Andrew Balding's filly finished sixth on debut over course and distance in Good ground with David Probert, who takes the ride again; her prominent style is flagged as out of natural role, but with nothing to press her she is likely to control this race wire-to-wire.

runners_data.name: Lilywhite Hart
runners_data.note: Dean Ivory's filly has twice finished mid-table over 6f on Good ground at a similar level; her unknown style profile (U) is a slight puzzle, but two runs at this trip suggest she is learning the job and J F Egan is a strong booking.

runners_data.name: Minkaas
runners_data.note: Placed third on debut over 5f on Good ground for T J Kent, whose 14-day record is a noteworthy 3/3; stepping up to 6f for Billy Loughnane, she has natural hold-up tendencies but only one career run — the trainer's hot short-term form is the angle to keep in mind.

runners_data.name: Pensando A Te
runners_data.note: Marco Botti's debutante for Marco Ghiani has no public form and an unknown going preference; she is lightly raced by definition and must be respected on reputation alone, though the going is flagged as unknown for her, adding uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Pure Majesty
runners_data.note: William Haggas sends out a filly who finished last (10th) on debut over 6f on Good ground with Tom Marquand; the fades-in-finish flag is a concern, and while the Haggas–Marquand combination demands respect, one poor run offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Speed of Sound
runners_data.note: Richard Spencer's filly has two consecutive placed efforts (2nd, 3rd) over course and distance on Good ground, giving her the strongest recent form profile in the race; Saffie Osborne takes the ride on a horse with a style unknown tag, but her solid course-distance record makes her a natural beneficiary of a steadily-run race.

races.paceDynamic: Lady Of Hay is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner maiden and, with no genuine rival willing or able to press her for the lead, she is set to bowl along at a controlled, uncontested tempo on Good to Firm ground at Yarmouth's flat, straight six furlongs. That measured pace will compress the field into a tight bunch from the early stages, limiting the advantage available to anything making a late run and making position off the bend-free track the decisive factor. The field carries more hold-up intent than the track can accommodate: Ava Louise, Babzini, Divine Concerto, Minkaas, Foxsbrush and Pure Majesty are all natural hold-up types, but with so many seeking the same rear positions only a handful will find clear daylight in time, and several will race closer to the pace than they prefer. This race shape strongly favours horses able to travel in the first half of the field and pick up smoothly off the steady gallop — a prominent-to-midfield tracking profile is the one to side with, as pure closers face a near-impossible task if Lady Of Hay is not stopping.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Track Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Of Hay dictates a measured pace and nothing mounts a serious challenge until the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Lady Of Hay controls every yard from her low draw, setting an honest but not punishing tempo that leaves her with energy to sustain through the final furlong; horses tracking in the first three lengths have first run and sweep past any faders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Trackers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slightly quicker than expected and those tracking in mid-division benefit from an even gallop.
scenarios.body: Speed of Sound and Lilywhite Hart, both with course-distance form, track the leader in a compact pack and quicken past a slightly-stretched Lady Of Hay inside the final furlong; their ability to handle this trip and going gives them the edge over rivals forced wider.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and a clear gap appears late for a hold-up runner to exploit.
scenarios.body: Minkaas or Babzini, getting an unusually clean passage from the rear, finds enough room on the stands rail to pick up late ground and grab a placing; however, the uncontested pace makes a truly end-to-end gallop unlikely, reducing the window for this shape to materialise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debutante Upsets Market
scenarios.trigger: If Pensando A Te on debut or Lilywhite Hart improves sharply on previous form and the field is caught flat-footed.
scenarios.body: An unexposed newcomer with unknown ceiling travels prominently, benefits from the undemanding early pace, and outstays the field with raw ability that form figures have not yet revealed; this scenario requires untapped improvement beyond what current evidence shows.

watchPoints.text: Lady Of Hay is the only horse setting the pace — if she gets an uncontested lead under David Probert and Yarmouth's fast ground suits, she could steal an unassailable advantage before the field realises the race has been run.

Speed of Sound is the best-qualified filly on course-and-distance form (two placings over 6f here on Good ground) and could prove the most dangerous if she tracks the leader from off a steady gallop — watch her position in the early stages.

Minkaas for T J Kent (3/3 over 14 days) should not be dismissed despite stepping up in trip; if the trainer's hot run of form reflects a horse ready to go, Billy Loughnane may push her forward rather than settle at the back where she is outnumbered by hold-up rivals.

The cluster of hold-up fillies — Ava Louise, Babzini, Divine Concerto, Foxsbrush, Pure Majesty — will be jostling for limited rear-field positions; crowding and interference from the wide draw are real risks, and any who cannot secure a clean passage are unlikely to land a blow from the back.

Pensando A Te is Botti's debutante and worth monitoring in the paddock and at the start — unexposed Botti two-year-olds on seasonal debut have surprised before, and with no form to anchor expectations her price may be underestimating raw ability.

races.name: Strawberry Fields Stud Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Dubai Charm
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes' filly brings strong recent form (win last time, placed twice) over similar going, races prominently and should find this drop back to 5f from 6f suits; 28 days fresh and going record of 3/4 in similar conditions makes her a natural threat close to the pace.|

runners_data.name: Beauty Box
runners_data.note: James Tate's filly wears headgear (hood) and holds an excellent record on Good ground (4/4 similar going), but 41 days off and a step back from 6f to 5f after a modest run last time warrants monitoring; her confirmed front-running role is the key tactical asset in this small field.|

runners_data.name: Wait Geordie
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's gelding has consistent 5f form on Good ground with a win and place from five runs on similar going, but the hold-up style in a five-runner field with a settled pace-setter is a structural challenge; three consecutive below-par efforts before last run temper expectations despite the trip suitability.|

runners_data.name: Troublesome Guest
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand takes the ride for George Margarson but the form string features an 0 in recent runs and the hold-up style mirrors Wait Geordie's problem — needing something to go wrong up front to get involved late; dropped trip from 6f to 5f is unproven and no wins from four similar-going starts.|

runners_data.name: Dowman
runners_data.note: George Boughey's colt arrives on a strong figure of three consecutive placed or winning runs at 5f on Good ground, and Billy Loughnane's booking is positive; the 65-day absence is the main uncertainty, but a prominent racing style means he will at least be competitive in the places from a handy position if fit.|

races.paceDynamic: Beauty Box is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no rival willing or able to contest the early lead, she will stride out uncontested from the gates and dictate a clean, controllable tempo over this flat Yarmouth 5f on Good to Firm ground. Dubai Charm and Dowman will press forward into prominent positions just off the leader, meaning the race will likely settle into a single-file procession with Beauty Box controlling the fractions. The two hold-up horses — Wait Geordie and Troublesome Guest — will be forced to produce their challenge from the rear of a five-runner field, where the covering ground and lack of a truly hot gallop may limit their ability to generate meaningful late momentum. This race shape strongly favours the prominent and pace-pressing profile: a comfortable, uncontested lead on fast ground over a sharp 5f is the optimal scenario for a horse who can dictate and quicken, with hold-up horses at a structural disadvantage against a relaxed front-runner in a small field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Beauty Box Leads Unopposed
scenarios.trigger: If Beauty Box breaks cleanly and controls a steady-to-fair tempo with no rival applying early pressure.
scenarios.body: She settles into her rhythm in front, makes every yard on the stands-side rail, and has enough in reserve to repel challengers in the final furlong on going that suits her profile. Prominent runners like Dubai Charm and Dowman who are close throughout are best placed to chase her down, but the uncontested lead gives her a significant tactical edge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Cuts Down Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Beauty Box's long lay-off (41 days) blunts her finishing effort and a pressing rival swoops in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: Dubai Charm, fresh from a recent win and racing prominently, or Dowman pressing from a handy position could capitalise if Beauty Box ties up late, with the prominent runners best equipped to inherit the momentum. Dowman's strong recent form profile and class at the trip make this the secondary plausible shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Finish Fast
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final furlong and Wait Geordie or Troublesome Guest generate a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: Wait Geordie has solid 5f form on this going and David Probert may time a late challenge if the front-runners overpace in a small field, but five runners and a controlled gallop make this a structurally difficult shape to execute. Troublesome Guest's modest form figures and 0 wins from similar going reduce confidence in this scenario landing.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Break Reshuffles Race
scenarios.trigger: If a poor start by Beauty Box eliminates her front-running advantage and forces an uncharacteristic scramble.
scenarios.body: In this unlikely scenario, the race loses its clear pace anchor and becomes a rough sprint to the line where any runner could emerge, particularly those closest to the rail. This is the least probable shape given Beauty Box's established pace profile and Hector Crouch's ability to position quickly.

watchPoints.text: Beauty Box's 41-day absence combined with the hood means her market move at the off is critical — if she drifts noticeably, her fitness may be questioned and Dubai Charm becomes more dangerous.|
Wait Geordie has run poorly in three consecutive outings at 5f on Good ground before a brief revival — if the pace is truly pedestrian he may never land a blow from the rear of only five runners.|
Dowman's 65-day lay-off is the longest in the field; if he shows any sign of rustiness in the stalls or the early stages, his prominent position could prove more of a burden than a benefit.|

Dubai Charm drops from 6f to 5f having won over 5f on Good ground on her most recent start — worth confirming her stall draw relative to Beauty Box, as rail position in a five-runner flat sprint at Yarmouth can influence the advantage she can press.|

Troublesome Guest's trainer George Margarson has only one booking in the past 14 days from nine runners — low-volume operation and modest recent form suggest managing expectations unless there is significant market support.|

races.name: Origin Amenity Solutions Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands C And D) (GBB Race)
Brandfords Restaurant & Bars Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Le Rouge Chinois
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up operator for Michael Appleby, returning from 104 days off, with a third over 16f on soft ground giving some staying credibility; wears headgear (p) and his best chance hinges on the pace being strong enough to set up a late run, which this race shape may not provide.

runners_data.name: Urban Warrior
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams' four-year-old has finished third or better in four of his last five starts including a placed effort over 14f on good ground, making him arguably the most in-form runner here; a genuine hold-up type whose recent 13-day turnaround and good-going record (2/7 on similar) give him solid claims if he can get a run through the pack.

runners_data.name: Highland Harvey
runners_data.note: Gihan Arnolda's four-year-old carries a natural hold-up style and a fade-in-finish flag, having contested mainly 12f races on good and standard ground where he has shown consistent mid-division form; he is pushed into a midfield mapping here by the crowded rear, and his STYLE_FIT of 0.92 suggests he is unlikely to produce his best racing out of his preferred position.

runners_data.name: Fornido
runners_data.note: Michael Attwater's four-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse who has finished second over 16f on standard ground and fourth on three other occasions at 14-16f, showing a consistent staying profile; returning from 131 days off and with just one win from 13 on similar going, the fitness question and the compressed pace shape both work against him.

runners_data.name: Regally Blonde
runners_data.note: Ben Case's seven-year-old has a strong record on good ground (12/15 runs on similar, including 2 wins and 4 places) and stays well over 16-18f, but she is a natural hold-up type pushed into a midfield role by the field's composition; the STYLE_FIT tag at 0.93 and the lack of a strong pace to chase into temper her appeal despite the excellent going match.

runners_data.name: Spaceage Love Song
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's four-year-old has placed twice over 12f on good ground with a pair of second-place finishes recently, suggesting she is hitting a vein of form; she wears headgear (p) and her natural preference for dropping in and finishing off her races means this steady gallop with a lone leader could leave her short of the pace she needs to build momentum.

runners_data.name: Cloudy Rose
runners_data.note: John Berry's eight-year-old is the only confirmed pace-setter in the race and will likely bowl along in front from the break over 1m6f without a single genuine rival to challenge her; her record of 2 wins and 3 places from 15 runs on similar going gives her meaningful course-type credentials, and Tom Marquand's booking adds tactical assurance, though her STYLE_FIT note signals she too will need to perform at the upper end of her ability.

races.paceDynamic: Cloudy Rose is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of seven over 1m6f on good-to-firm ground at Yarmouth, and with no genuine rival to push her early, she can bowl along at a controlled, unhurried gallop from the outset. The remainder of the field — Le Rouge Chinois, Urban Warrior, Highland Harvey, Fornido, Regally Blonde, and Spaceage Love Song — are all hold-up types by nature, meaning the pace Cloudy Rose sets is unlikely to be seriously tested from behind. This creates a race likely run at a steady, manageable tempo that will compress the field and make it genuinely difficult for true closers to generate the momentum they need in the straight. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear, with Highland Harvey, Fornido, Regally Blonde, and Spaceage Love Song all redistributed to midfield — Cloudy Rose is most likely to actually secure her position at the front, with Le Rouge Chinois and Urban Warrior the most plausible candidates to travel just behind. The tactical verdict is clear: front-running and prominent profiles benefit most here, as a moderate gallop set by an uncontested leader on a flat track heavily favours those who can control the race from the front and quicken in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cloudy Rose Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Cloudy Rose is allowed to coast in front at a steady clip with no rival willing or able to pressurise her through the middle portions of the race.
scenarios.body: Cloudy Rose dictates on her own terms over 1m6f, conserving energy through the long Yarmouth straight before kicking again in the final two furlongs; with hold-up horses unable to generate a meaningful sweeping run from rear, a patient leader who has controlled every yard is hard to peg back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the middle stages, creating a false-pace scenario where the gap between the leader and the chasing pack narrows enough for the better-quality closers to challenge.
scenarios.body: A true hold-up horse who has been travelling sweetly in the slipstream accelerates past a weakening Cloudy Rose inside the final furlong on the fast ground; this scenario requires the pace to be genuinely slow enough to allow closers to build momentum without cover.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Improver Picks Up
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest enough through the first mile to string the field out and create a platform for a sustained late run from midfield.
scenarios.body: One of the redistributed hold-up types, travelling in what is actually their preferred position in the middle of the pack, benefits from a flat track and fast ground to pick up when asked two furlongs out; Spaceage Love Song and Highland Harvey, both with recent decent form at shorter distances, are the most plausible beneficiaries here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Scrappy Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is so dawdling that the race degenerates into a sprint finish with the entire field bunched entering the straight.
scenarios.body: With seven hold-up types and one front-runner, a stop-start gallop could produce a chaotic shake-up where the highest-rated horse or the one with the best turn of foot prevails regardless of position; Urban Warrior and Le Rouge Chinois, with the best recent form, are best positioned to capitalise in a contested sprint finish.

watchPoints.text: Cloudy Rose — watch how quickly she establishes the lead from the gates; if she finds herself unchallenged within the first two furlongs and sets a truly dawdling tempo, hold-up horses behind her may never generate the pace differential needed to reel her in.

Le Rouge Chinois — returning from a 104-day absence and dropping back from softer ground; watch the market moves pre-race as any significant support would suggest the Appleby yard has him fit enough to produce a sharp return over a staying trip.

Highland Harvey — flagged as a horse who fades in the finish, yet mapped to midfield due to the crowded hold-up group; watch whether Billy Loughnane pushes him forward early to avoid that positional compromise, which would alter the pace dynamic unexpectedly.

Spaceage Love Song — her two recent second-place finishes over 10-12f on good ground suggest she is in form, but watch whether the step up to 1m6f on a flat track suits a horse who has not yet won and whose last outing over 14f produced a seventh.

Fornido — 131 days off the track is a significant layoff for a hold-up horse with limited wins on similar going; watch whether market confidence builds in the final hour, as Michael Attwater will need him to be spot-on physically to have a realistic chance on this pace map.

races.name: Bet Central Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Banana
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old confirmed front-runner for Scott Dixon who has recent placed form at 5f on Good ground and drops back in class here; tp headgear confirms the bold-going intent and the 33-day break looks manageable — the key question is whether Pure Passion simply won't let her dictate.

runners_data.name: Cabeza De Llave
runners_data.note: Attwater's seven-year-old has five consecutive runs on Good ground at 5f and clearly has the course-distance profile, but this horse's natural instinct is to be ridden from the rear and with several hold-up types in the field it will struggle to get that position — tempering confidence accordingly.

runners_data.name: Charging Bull
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand takes the ride on this four-year-old who has placed at 5f on softer ground; no wins over this configuration but the ht headgear suggests connections want him switched on and a tracking role just off the pace could suit if the front-runners cut each other up.

runners_data.name: Chiedozie
runners_data.note: Veteran five-year-old whose form string reads -08990 and whose last five runs produce double-figure finishes on Good and Standard; runs in a visor, and although this horse's instinct is to race from the back, the form simply isn't there to suggest a revival even with positional luck.

runners_data.name: She Went Whoosh
runners_data.note: Dixon's four-year-old holds tp headgear and has a single placed run at 6f on Good ground among mostly disappointing efforts; a true hold-up type who will find herself shuffled further forward than ideal in this shape, and a recent run of six consecutive mid-pack finishes makes involvement hard to construct.

runners_data.name: Mayflower Rock
runners_data.note: Three-year-old lightly raced filly for Cunha who is stepping back to 5f after a 7f start on Good ground; only four career runs leaves questions open but the sample is thin enough that inexperience cuts both ways, and with a 132lbs claim she could represent some value if her form line understates her.

runners_data.name: Pure Passion
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams's three-year-old is a confirmed front-runner who has raced 5f on Standard ground previously and steps onto turf here; Chloe Lyons takes a 7lb claim and the horse has shown placing ability at this trip — the burning question is how long she can hold on once the Good to Firm surface tests her stamina in the final 100 yards.

runners_data.name: Shining Guest
runners_data.note: Margarson's three-year-old has consistent finishes in the 5-7 bracket on Good ground at 6f and 7f, but dropping to 5f on turf feels like a trip that is sharp of her best; with 40 days since last run and no win on the board, she is hard to place prominently in any scenario.

races.paceDynamic: Pure Passion and Banana are the two confirmed front-runners in this eight-runner 5f sprint at Yarmouth, and with both likely to push for the lead from the gates, the pace will be genuinely contested from the off rather than a controlled procession. The going report confirms Good to Firm conditions for the 8:10, which suits horses who can travel fluently on fast ground without being anchored. This honest, competitive early tempo tends to drain the reserves of the pace-setters in the final furlong and marginally favours horses who can race prominently without burning their petrol chasing for the lead — sitting just off a genuine pace rather than making it. The field carries far more hold-up intent than the track can accommodate: Cabeza De Llave, She Went Whoosh, Shining Guest, and Chiedozie are all true rear-of-field types displaced into midfield by the shape, meaning they are unlikely to operate from their natural position and the scenario that relies on a true late surge from deep is structurally compromised from the start.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Pure Passion or Banana seizes the lead cleanly and the pace stays controlled enough for one of them to maintain momentum into the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Pure Passion has shown the ability to get her position on 5f turf and Banana has recent placed form over this course configuration, so a dominant front-running display from either on fast ground is credible; Good to Firm conditions reward horses who can roll along without being stopped in their tracks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners push each other hard and a horse sitting just off the lead in second or third is able to sprint past the tiring leaders inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The contested gallop from Pure Passion and Banana sets up a classic 5f scenario where a horse racing close but conserving a fraction of energy inherits the race; Charging Bull has shown 5f placed form on soft-ish and standard ground and could find the quicker surface liberating from a tracking berth.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly burning and the front-runners tie each other up enough to allow a horse from further back to pick them off close home.
scenarios.body: Cabeza De Llave has shown consistent ability to figure in 5f Good-ground finishes and is the most naturally gifted of those displaced from their true hold-up position, but the STYLE_FIT concern and redistribution mean this scenario is structurally less likely than the map implies; She Went Whoosh would also need things to fall perfectly after mixed recent form.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Upsets
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at a chaotic pace and an unconsidered runner catches the field in a moment of positional confusion.
scenarios.body: Shining Guest has consistent form on Good ground at 6f and dropping to 5f is a concern, while Mayflower Rock is lightly raced and unexposed enough to spring a surprise if her trainer's 2-from-28 strike rate is an understatement of her readiness; Chiedozie's very poor recent form makes involvement negligible.

watchPoints.text: Pure Passion and Banana are both confirmed front-runners — watch the first furlong closely to see which one blinks first, as the outcome of that duel will define whether either survives to the line or collapses in the final 100 yards.

Cabeza De Llave is a true hold-up horse mapped into midfield by the race shape — if Seamus Cronin tries to push forward to compensate, it could produce uncharacteristic erratic early positioning and interference risk for nearby runners.

Charging Bull is fitted with ht headgear suggesting a known tendency to idle or pull; in a fast-run sprint with Tom Marquand trying to track, any early over-enthusiasm could see him spend his race by halfway.

Taryn Langley claims 5lbs for Banana — on a night when the going is Good to Firm and margins will be tight, the weight relief is material but the combination of a claim rider and a front-running hold-it-together assignment is worth monitoring for timing in the final furlong.

The going report lists all races on the card as Good to Firm despite the race card advertising Good — the faster surface will compress the finish and reduce the window for any horse coming from off the pace, further narrowing the hold-up horses' already compromised chances.
